seoTitle: Markup Calculator - Calculate Selling Price & Profit
metaDescription: Free markup calculator. Easily find your final selling price, gross profit, and profit margin by entering your cost and desired markup percentage.
intro: Setting the right price for your products is crucial for business success. Our Markup Calculator helps you determine the exact selling price needed to achieve your desired profit. Understanding how to calculate markup correctly is essential for maintaining a healthy bottom line. Incorrect pricing can lead to lost sales if too high, or unmanageable losses if too low. By using our tool, you eliminate the guesswork and ensure your business operations are grounded in accurate financial data. Consistent and deliberate pricing methods are the foundation of sustainable retail and wholesale businesses. This tool provides the clarity you need to set prices confidently, ensuring every sale contributes positively to your overall business objectives and long-term financial health.
whatIs: This tool is a financial calculator that takes your cost of goods sold (COGS) and a markup percentage to determine the final selling price, gross profit, and equivalent profit margin.
howToUse: Enter the Cost of your product or service.
The tool will instantly display the target Selling Price.
It also calculates your Gross Profit in currency and your true Profit Margin as a percentage.
howItWorks: The tool multiplies the cost by the markup percentage to find the gross profit. It then adds this profit to the original cost to determine the selling price. Finally, it divides the gross profit by the selling price to find the profit margin.
workedExample: If your cost is $50 and you apply a 100% markup: The gross profit is $50 (50 * 1.00). The selling price becomes $100. The equivalent profit margin is 50% ($50 / $100).
resultInterpretation: The Selling Price is what you should charge your customers. Gross Profit is the raw amount of money you make on the sale. Profit Margin shows what percentage of the final sale price is actual profit.
useCases: Retailers: Pricing wholesale inventory for retail sale.
Contractors: Adding a standard markup to materials used on a job.
Manufacturers: Ensuring the selling price covers production costs plus profit.
tipsAndLimitations: A common mistake is confusing markup and margin. A 50% markup does NOT equal a 50% margin.
This tool calculates based on gross numbers, not net (which includes operating expenses).

faq.question: What is the difference between markup and margin?
faq.answer: Markup is the percentage you add to the COST to reach the selling price. Margin is the percentage of the SELLING PRICE that represents your profit.

faq.question: Why is margin always lower than markup?
faq.answer: Because margin is calculated against the higher selling price, while markup is calculated against the lower cost price. For example, a 100% markup always yields a 50% margin.

cta: Calculate your markup and selling price now!
